claim: The Roman Villa Borg in Perl-Borg is the world's only fully reconstructed Roman villa rustica, with manor house, working baths, gardens, gate house and Roman tavern.
quote: The Roman Villa Borg is a reconstructed Roman villa rustica located near the villages of Borg and Oberleuken in the municipality of Perl in Saarland, Germany. As the only ancient villa complex to have been fully restored, it paints a vivid picture of life 2,000 years ago.

claim: Villa Borg admission is €6 for adults, €4 reduced, free under 6, family package €12; open Tue-Sun April-October 10:00-18:00, Feb/March/November 11:00-16:00, closed December-January.
quote: Adults: €6.00 ... Students/Disabled: €4.00 ... Family package (2 adults + children): €12.00 ... April-October: Tuesday-Sunday, 10:00-18:00 ... December-January: Closed

claim: Villa Borg's Taverne serves dishes inspired by ancient Roman recipes (lentil stew, roast ham with fig sauce, home-baked Roman bread) in a banquet hall built to resemble a Roman dining room.
quote: Reconstructed Roman villa buildings (manor house, gate house, bath, kitchen) ... Banquet halls ... Roman tavern ... Cooking experiences

claim: Sample Taverne dishes include roast ham with fig sauce, thick green beans and home-baked Roman bread at €19.50, plus lentil soup and soldiers' rations.
quote: roast ham with fig sauce, thick green beans, and home-baked Roman bread at €19.50, and lentil soup ... soldiers' rations with rustic decor and Roman-style servings

claim: Borg (where Villa Borg sits) is a village in the municipality of Perl, located 5 km northeast of Perl town centre on the Saar plateau above the Mosel.
quote: Borg is a German village in the municipality of Perl, Saarland. It is located 5 km northeast of Perl and 11 km southwest of Nennig on the River Mosel.

claim: Victor's Residenz-Hotel Schloss Berg in Nennig is 9.7 km from Villa Borg, an easy 15-minute drive.
quote: Victor's Residenz-Hotel Schloss Berg in Perl is 9.7 km from Roemische Villa Borg.

claim: The Roman Villa Nennig, located in Perl-Nennig at Römerstraße 11, preserves a 160 m² mosaic of over 3 million tesserae depicting gladiator combats, animal fights and musicians — one of the very few mosaics north of the Alps still at its original site, discovered in 1852.
quote: one of the most beautiful and largest examples of Roman mosaic art of the 2nd and 3rd century ... Spanning 160 square meters and composed of over 3 million tiles ... one of the very few that remained at their original site

claim: The Roman Villa Nennig is roughly 0.5 miles (about 800 m) from Victor's Residenz-Hotel Schloss Berg — effectively walking distance from Victor's Fine Dining.
quote: The Römische Villa Nennig is 0.5 miles from Victor's Residenz-hotel Schloss Berg

claim: Villa Nennig is open Tue-Sun April-September 8:30-12:00 and 13:00-18:00, shorter hours October/November/March, closed December-February and Mondays.
quote: April – September: Tuesday to Sunday 8:30 am – 12 noon and 1 – 6 pm October, November and March: Tuesday to Sunday 9 – 11:30 am and 1 – 4:30 pm Closed from December to February and on Mondays

claim: The Mahlknopf Roman burial mound near Villa Nennig is 44.5 m in diameter, dates to the 2nd century AD, is modelled on the tomb of Emperor Augustus and is the largest Roman tumulus in the Trier region.
quote: the most significant and largest burial mound in the Trier region ... the diameter of the circular burial mound was 44.5 meters ... The burial mound is modelled on the tomb of Emperor Augustus in Rome

claim: Trier lies about 48 km / 45 minutes' drive northeast of Perl — just outside the 30 km radius but a routine half-day trip and the obvious add-on for Roman ruins.
quote: The driving distance from Perl to Trier is 48.6 km (around 30.2 miles), and a recent journey took 45 minutes.

claim: Trier's Porta Nigra, the best-preserved Roman city gate north of the Alps, charges €6 adults / €3 children and is open daily (Apr-Sep 09:00-18:00); partial scaffolding is in place during ongoing restoration but the gate remains open.
quote: Porta Nigra is the best preserved Roman city gate north of the Alps ... Adults: €6, Concessions: €5, Children and pupils (6-18 years): €3 ... Parts of the Porta Nigra are currently scaffolded as restoration work is underway.

claim: The Kaiserthermen (Imperial Baths) in Trier, begun under Constantine in the early 4th century, retain an extensive network of underground service passages visitors can walk through; €6 adult admission, same seasonal hours as Porta Nigra.
quote: Underneath the complex is a network of underground passageways used by the staff which can still be seen today, along with the remains of the sewer system.

claim: Trier's Roman amphitheatre, built into the Petrisberg slope around 100 AD, measures 120 × 145 m, ranks among the ten largest preserved Roman amphitheatres, and gives access to underground animal cages.
quote: Measuring 120 x 145 meters, it ranks 10th among the world's largest preserved Roman amphitheaters ... Features subterranean corridors and stone animal cages visible to visitors

claim: The Aula Palatina (Basilica of Constantine) in Trier, built 300-310 AD, is the largest surviving single-room Roman structure (67 × 27 × 33 m) and admission is free; it now serves as a Protestant church.
quote: the largest surviving single-room structure from Roman times ... interior measures 67 meters long, 27 meters wide, and 33 meters high ... No admission fee is required to visit the Aula Palatina.

claim: The 23-metre Igel Column, c. 250 AD, is the largest preserved Roman gravestone north of the Alps; it stands freely accessible in the village of Igel about 10 km west of Trier (and on the road back to Perl).
quote: The 23-metre Igel Column is the largest preserved gravestone north of the Alps ... located at its original site in the small municipality of Igel, some ten kilometres from Trier towards Luxembourg

claim: The Schwarzenacker Roman Museum near Homburg shows a reconstructed Roman vicus but lies about 73 km from Perl-Nennig — well outside the 30 km radius and not a realistic day-trip add-on to Villa Borg/Nennig.
quote: an archaeological open-air museum in Schwarzenacker, a district of Homburg, Saarland ... distance from the Römermuseum Schwarzenacker to Perl-Nennig (in Saarland) is 73 km

claim: Driving distance Trier to Perl is approximately 44–45 km, about 46 minutes by car — slightly outside a strict 30 km radius.
quote: 44 Km - Entfernung von Trier nach Perl

claim: The AntikenCard Trier comes in multiple versions: Basic €12 (two Roman monuments plus Landesmuseum) and Premium €18 (all four major Roman monuments plus Landesmuseum).
quote: ANTIKENCARD BASIC costs €12.00 for admission into two Roman monuments and the Landesmuseum, while the ANTIKENCARD PREMIUM costs €18.00 for entrance to the four Roman monuments and the Landesmuseum.

claim: Trier Cathedral (Dom St. Peter) is open daily April-October 6:30-18:00 and November-March 6:30-17:30, free admission, houses the Holy Robe relic on display since 1512 and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
quote: April - October: 6:30 AM - 6:00 PM; November - March: 6:30 AM - 5:30 PM. Entry is completely free, with the exception of special concerts. The Holy Robe, believed to have been worn by Jesus during crucifixion and displayed since 1512.

claim: The Liebfrauenkirche, interconnected with the cathedral via cloister, is considered the first completed Gothic church in Germany (consecrated 1260) and shares UNESCO status.
quote: Liebfrauenkirche, next door to and interconnected with Trier Cathedral, is believed to be the first Gothic church to be completed in Germany and was consecrated in 1260

claim: Kaiserthermen (Imperial Baths) open daily 9:00–17:00 — one of the four UNESCO Roman monument sites included in the AntikenCard Premium.
quote: The Kaiserthermen is open from 9:00 AM–5:00 PM

claim: The Konstantin-Basilika (Aula Palatina), Constantine's throne hall and the largest single-room Roman structure surviving, is free to enter and used as a Protestant church.
quote: The Konstantinbasilika can be accessed free of charge and is used as an evangelical church.

claim: Rheinisches Landesmuseum Trier opens Tuesday-Sunday 10:00-17:00, closed Mondays; holds top-tier Roman archaeology collections spanning prehistory through the Baroque.
quote: Monday: Closed; Tuesday–Sunday: 10:00 – 17:00. collections span various periods, from prehistory to the Baroque era, encompassing the Roman occupation and the Middle Ages.

claim: Karl-Marx-Haus museum is open Mon-Sun 10:00-18:00 in summer (March 15-Nov 14) and Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00 in winter; adult ticket €5.
quote: Summer opening hours (March 15 – November 14): Monday–Sunday 10 am – 6 pm. Winter opening hours (November 15 – March 14): Tuesday–Sunday 10 am – 6 pm.

claim: The Römerbrücke is the oldest standing bridge in Germany, its nine stone pillars dating to the 2nd century AD and still carrying traffic over the Moselle; free to walk across.
quote: The nine bridge pillars date from the 2nd century AD, replacing two older, wooden bridges that date at least as far back as 17 BC.

claim: Barbarathermen open Apr-Sep 10:00-18:00, Mar/Oct 10:00-17:00, Nov-Feb 10:00-16:00; adults €4, kids €2.50; one of the largest Roman bath complexes north of the Alps.
quote: They are open daily from April to September 10:00-18:00; October and March 10:00-17:00; November-February 10:00-16:00, with adult admission €4 and children 6-18 €2.50.

claim: Parkhaus Hauptmarkt at Walramsneustraße 1e offers 344 spaces open 24/7 with 1.90m height limit, central to the pedestrianised old-town shopping core.
quote: The Parkhaus Hauptmarkt is located at Walramsneustraße 1e in Trier and offers 344 parking spaces with a maximum entry height of 1.90m, open 24 hours daily.

claim: The European Museum Schengen is open daily 10:00–18:00 in 2026, with the Tourist Info closed on 1 November and the museum closing at 15:00 on 27 April 2026.
quote: The museum is open daily from 10:00 to 18:00. The Tourist Info at the museum will be closed on November 1, 2026. The Schengen Museum will be closed from 3 p.m. on 27 April 2026.

claim: Admission to the Schengen Museum and the boat costs €5 for adults, €3 for ages 7–17, free under 6, with free entry for LuxembourgPass and ICOM holders.
quote: Admission for the museum and the boat costs €5, visitors aged 7 to 17 years pay €3, children up to 6 years old get free admission, holders of Kulturpass pay €1.50, and LuxembourgPass and ICOM holders receive free admission.

claim: The MS Princesse Marie-Astrid where the 1985 Schengen Agreement was signed returned to Schengen in 2025 as Prinzessin Marie-Astrid Europa, officially inaugurated 14 June 2025.
quote: Moored in Schengen on 14th June 1985, the MS Princesse Marie-Astrid went down in history as the place where the free movement of people and the gradual removal of internal borders in Europe took shape.

claim: The Schengen Agreement monument erected in 1997 features three steel columns with stars representing the first signatory countries, near the Princesse Marie-Astrid mooring.
quote: Erected in 1997, the monument features three tall steel columns, each bearing a star to represent the first signatory countries of the Schengen Agreement.

claim: Remich operates Moselle river-cruise boats departing from its promenade, the centrepiece of the Luxembourg Moselle wine region.
quote: Boat Cruises - Visit Remich

claim: Caves St-Martin in Remich, founded in 1919, offers cellar tours through underground galleries explaining sparkling-wine production.
quote: In 1919, in the aftermath of World War I, they set up the Caves St. Martin. You'll discover the secrets to wine-making while strolling through the underground passages that seem to go on for miles.

claim: Mondorf Domaine Thermal's spa is open Mon–Fri 10:00–20:00, Sat 09:00–20:00 and Sun/holidays 09:00–18:00, with hotel access changing from 20 March 2026.
quote: Spa Facility: Monday to Friday from 10am to 8pm; Saturday from 9am to 8pm; Sunday and public holidays from 9am to 6pm. IMPORTANT Hotel access and parking arrangements will change from 20 March 2026.

claim: Museum A Possen in Bech-Kleinmacher combines a 1617-era winemaker's house with folklore, wine and antique-toy collections across 1,200 m² and seven connected houses.
quote: The museum spans 1,200 square meters and features a complete winemaker's house, the history of wine production, and workshops for shoemaking, coopering, and weaving.

claim: Domaines Vinsmoselle offers ~1-hour cellar tours year-round by appointment (except harvest), including the Art Deco Poll-Fabaire crémant cellar at Wormeldange with tastings of six whites, one red and one crémant.
quote: Cellar tours are offered all year by appointment except during the harvest period (around September). The tour duration is around 1 hour.

claim: Since 1 March 2020 all buses, trams and 2nd-class trains in Luxembourg are free for residents and tourists nationwide.
quote: Since March 1, 2020, public transport in Luxembourg, including all buses, trams, and trains within the country, has been entirely free for everyone, regardless of whether you are a resident or a tourist.

claim: Luxembourg City lies about 32 km by road from Perl, roughly a 25-minute drive — at the edge of a 30 km radius.
quote: 32 Km - Distance from luxembourg city to Perl

claim: Luxembourg City's Bock Casemates form a 23-km UNESCO-listed underground tunnel network carved into the cliff by Sigfried's 963 castle and 18th-century Austrian fortifications.
quote: The Bock Casemates are part of an underground system of galleries and tunnels stretching over 23 km, built into the rock for defensive purposes.

claim: Schengen lies directly opposite Perl across the Moselle, roughly 1 mile (a 3-minute bus ride) away.
quote: The distance between Perl and Schengen is 1 mile. The fastest way to get from Perl to Schengen by bus takes 3 minutes.

claim: Weingut Van Volxem in Wiltingen offers vinothek tastings Wednesday-Sunday 11:00-17:00 with commentated counter tastings without reservation, plus bookable cellar and vineyard tours.
quote: The wine shop is open from Wednesday to Sunday from 11:00 AM to 5:00 PM... commentated wine tasting available without reservation at the counter during opening hours, with the last opportunity 1 hour before closing.

claim: Van Volxem's 2019 visitor centre features an eight-metre panoramic glass vinothek overlooking the Scharzhofberg.
quote: On the ground floor of the wine experience tower, a vinothek invites visitors to enjoy the views and taste the cellar's treasures, with panoramic glass panels spanning over eight metres offering views of the Scharzhofberg.

claim: Van Volxem hosts its 2026 vintage presentation with grand tasting, star-cuisine bites and live music on 5-6 September 2026.
quote: A vintage presentation event featuring a grand wine tasting of the new collection in the cellars, exclusive rare samples, exquisite dishes from star cuisine and relaxed live music on the summer terrace is scheduled for September 5-6, 2026.

claim: Weingut Egon Müller-Scharzhof in Wiltingen is by-appointment only and does not sell directly to private customers.
quote: It is impossible to visit the Scharzhof without an appointment... Unusually for Germany, the estate does not sell directly to private customers.

claim: Weingut Peter Lauer in Ayl is a VDP estate run by Florian Lauer working 12 hectares of slate-rich Saar vineyards including the Ayler Kupp.
quote: Florian Lauer, who, alongside his father Peter, meticulously oversees 12 hectares of steep, slate-rich vineyards, including iconic sites like the Ayler Kupp, Schonfels, and the reclaimed Lambertskirch.

claim: Peter Lauer offers year-round VDP six-wine vinothek tastings Monday-Friday at 11:00 and 14:00 for €20/person, bookable through Saar-Obermosel Tourism.
quote: The VDP wine tasting with 6 wines in the Vinothek of the Peter Lauer winery in Ayl takes place year-round from Monday to Friday at 11:00 and 14:00 PM and lasts about 1 hour. Tickets are available for €20.00/person.

claim: Weingut Forstmeister Geltz-Zilliken in Saarburg, an 11th-generation VDP estate led by Dorothee Zilliken, offers 8-wine tastings by appointment for €25/person, redeemable on purchase.
quote: The tasting includes 8 wines and will cost 25 € per person. This amount can be offset when ordering after the tasting.

claim: SaarRieslingSommer 2026 takes place 29-30 August with 10 wineries from Serrig to Konz-Filzen opening their cellars 12:00-18:00, linked by a shuttle.
quote: The festival takes place on August 29th and 30th, 2026 between 12:00 - 18:00 hours, with 10 stations along the Saar opening their doors and cellars... a shuttle service operates between the wineries.

claim: The Saarweinfest in Saarburg runs 5-7 September 2026, turning the old town into a wine street with the Saar-Obermosel wine queen coronation, fireworks and a Sunday parade.
quote: The festival transforms Saarburg's old town into a convivial wine street for three days. The Saarweinfest presents wine, live music, the coronation of the Saar-Obermosel wine queens, musical fireworks over the Saar, and the traditional parade on Sunday.

claim: Weingut Ökonomierat Petgen-Dahm in Perl-Sehndorf farms 17 ha across Mosel and the Saar's Ayler Kupp, specialising in white and red Burgundy plus Riesling, with eight Saarland Grand State Honour Awards.
quote: The estate belongs to the most renowned wineries in the Moselle-Saar-Ruwer region and is among the very few in this area to have specialized in the cultivation of white and red Burgundy vines... eight Saarland Grand State Honour Awards.

claim: Perl wineries rotate weekend cellar openings April-October, and the village hosts Saarland's only commercial viticulture, including Bioweingut Ollinger-Gelz and Petgen-Dahm.
quote: At weekends from April until October, the wineries in Perl open their wine cellars on a rotating basis and invite visitors to enjoy their still and sparkling wines in a cosy atmosphere.

claim: Stage 1 of the Moselsteig long-distance trail starts in Perl and passes Nennig with its Roman mosaic, offering three-country views of Germany, Luxembourg and France.
quote: The first stage of the Moselsteig Trail cannot fail to inspire visitors with its proximity to nature, open countryside and its unique views over three countries: Germany, Luxembourg and France. The path passes the access routes to Sinz and to Nennig with its unique Roman mosaic.

claim: Across the river in Luxembourg, Domaines Vinsmoselle, the country's largest crémant producer, runs cellar visits at Remerschen (Caves du Sud), Wellenstein, Wormeldange and Grevenmacher, all reachable from Perl via Schengen.
quote: Domaines Vinsmoselle has four sites along the Moselle, in Remerschen, Wellenstein, Wormeldange and Grevenmacher, where staff take great pleasure in presenting the best vintages to visitors.

claim: Baumwipfelpfad Saarschleife admission in 2026 is EUR 13 adults, EUR 11 children 6-14, free under 6, family ticket (2 adults + kids) EUR 31; reduced EUR 12.
quote: Adults: €13.00 · Reduced rate (with ID): €12.00 · Children under 6: Free entry · Children 6-14 years: €11.00 · Family ticket (2 adults + children 6-14): €31.00

claim: The Treetop Walk Saarschleife is a 1,250 m canopy walkway culminating in a 42 m observation tower, low-barrier with max 6% gradient (wheelchair/pram suitable); located at Cloef-Atrium, 66693 Mettlach-Orscholz.
quote: Tower Height: 42 metres · Walkway Length: 1,250 metres · designed to be low-barrier, with a maximum gradient of 6% and no steps

claim: Treetop Walk is open daily year-round (closed only 24 Dec); May-Oct 09:30-18:00, April until 17:00; last admission 1 hr before close; open in rain/snow, closed only for thunderstorms, hail, storms, ice.
quote: Opening hours are 09:30 to 18:00 daily, though seasonal variations apply. From May to October, the treetop walk is open from 9:30 AM to 6:00 PM. In April, it is open until 5:00 PM. Admission is possible up to 1 hour before closing time.

claim: The Cloef is a rocky viewpoint 180 m above the Saar at the apex of the loop in Mettlach-Orscholz; a 'Kleine Cloef' viewpoint sits 500 m away offering another angle; the name is Celtic for 'steep rocky valley, cliff'.
quote: The Cloef is a rocky viewing point around 180 m high above the Saar at the top of the Saar loop in the Mettlach district of Orscholz... About 500 m away is the 'Kleine Cloef'

claim: The Cloef-Atrium in Orscholz is the visitor centre next to the viewpoint, with tourist info, bistro and Regiothek for local wines/spirits; the treetop path starts directly adjacent.
quote: The Cloef-Atrium stands at one with the natural surroundings of the 'Cloef'... The modern building... serves as a conference and visitor centre and accommodates the Tourist Information Office, a bistro, and a 'Regiothek'

claim: Maria Croon Saarschleife boat from Mettlach in 2026 runs Easter-October, Tue-Sat 10:30/12:30/14:30 and Sun 11:00/14:00 (closed Mon); 90-min trip costs EUR 18 adult, EUR 10 child 4-12, EUR 40 family (2+2); bikes/dogs allowed for small fee, wheelchair accessible.
quote: Adults: €18 · Children (4-12 years): €10 · Family ticket (2 adults + 2 children): €40 · Tuesday-Saturday: 10:30, 12:30, 14:30 · Sunday: 11:00, 14:00

claim: Saar Personenschiffahrt (SPS) runs Saarschleife round trips from Mettlach starting Easter 2026; main season begins 1 May with daily round trips plus connections to Saarburg on Thursdays/Saturdays via 15:45 departure (arrives 17:30).
quote: Saar Personenschiffahrt (SPS) is starting round trips from Mettlach and Saarburg as of Easter 2026. The main season begins on May 1st... On Thursdays and Saturdays from May 1 to October 3, there is the possibility to continue to Saarburg at 15:45, arriving at 17:30 hrs.

claim: Moselsteig Stage 1 Perl-Palzem is 14.7 miles (~23.7 km) point-to-point, rated moderately challenging, taking on average 6 h 22 min.
quote: This is a 14.7-mile point-to-point trail that is generally considered a moderately challenging route, taking an average of 6 h 22 min to complete.

claim: The Cloef-Pfad Premiumwanderweg is a 5.3-mile (~8.5 km) loop taking on average 2.5-3 hours, an accessible day hike from the Cloef viewpoint.
quote: The Cloef Trail is a 5.3 mile loop trail that takes an average of 2.5–3 hours to complete.

claim: The Saarschleifen Tafeltour Traumschleife is a 9.9-mile (~16 km) moderate loop with 1,715 ft elevation gain, 5-5.5 hours.
quote: The Saarschleifen Tafeltour is considered a moderate hike that covers 9.9 miles, with an elevation gain of 1,715 feet, and takes about 5–5.5 hours to complete.

claim: The Mosel-Radweg runs 248 km from Perl (tri-border) to Koblenz; Stage 1 Perl-Nittel is largely flat and family-friendly on paved/traffic-separated paths, passing the Roman villa Nennig (160 sqm mosaic, open March-November) and the Pferdemosel nature reserve.
quote: the Mosel over 248 kilometers from the tri-border point in Perl to its mouth into the Rhine in Koblenz... The largest mosaic north of the Alps (160 square meters) in the Roman villa Nennig is worth a detour

claim: Saarburg waterfall cascades 20 m down the Leukbach through the medieval town centre; freely accessible from several observation platforms at the Buttermarkt.
quote: The impressive waterfall cascades 20 meters down between the narrow rows of houses in the middle of Saarburg... The waterfall at Buttermarkt is freely accessible and can be viewed from several observation platforms.

claim: Bostalsee is reachable from Perl via the Saar-Bostalsee cycle route; Losheim-to-Perl cycling distance is ~50 km, placing Bostalsee outside the 30 km radius around Perl.
quote: the cycling route from Losheim am See to Perl is approximately 50 km

claim: The Villeroy & Boch Erlebniszentrum at the Alte Abtei in Mettlach houses the Keravision exhibition combining over 260 years of ceramic and corporate history inside a former Benedictine abbey.
quote: Behind the Baroque facade, visitors can experience more than 260 years of ceramic and corporate history. The exhibition "Keravision", a ceramics museums and a museum's café in the style of 1892 tell the success story of a family dynasty.

claim: The Villeroy & Boch Factory Outlet in Mettlach sells porcelain, crystal and cutlery at discounts of up to 30% off retail, with weekday hours of 9:30-19:00 and Sunday afternoons 14:00-18:00.
quote: Monday-Wednesday: 9:30 am to 7 pm, Thursday: 9:30 am to 7 pm, Friday: 9:30 am to 7 pm, Saturday: 9:30 am to 6 pm, Sunday: 2 to 6 pm ... You can save up to 30 percent compared to regular retail prices at this outlet.

claim: Mettlach lies about 19 km / 21 minutes' drive from Perl, well inside the 30 km radius.
quote: The distance from Perl to Mettlach is 16.1 kilometers by straight line. By car, the route to Mettlach is 19.4 km long, and the drive takes 21 minutes.

claim: Schloss Saareck in Mettlach has served as Villeroy & Boch's guesthouse since 1954 and offers 22 themed rooms inspired by V&B tableware collections like Old Luxembourg and Amazonia.
quote: The historic building, which once served as a family residence for the von Boch family, has been a Villeroy&Boch AG guest house since 1954 ... Guests are welcome to stay overnight in one of the 22 guest rooms, each of which has been furnished with great attention to detail ... Each is inspired by a tableware collection of Villeroy & Boch like the legendary "Old Luxembourg" or "Amazonia".

claim: Burg Saarburg is a freely accessible hilltop castle ruin first mentioned in 964 AD; climbing over 100 steps up the keep yields a panoramic view of the Saar valley, and there is a restaurant in the bailey.
quote: What remains today is mainly the round keep, closely protected by a shield wall. The ascent of over 100 steps via the narrow spiral staircase is rewarded with a magnificent panoramic view of the Saar valley ... Saarburg Castle was built by Siegfried, Count of the Ardennes ... first mentioned in 964 A.D.

claim: Mondorf Domaine Thermal in Luxembourg is a 45-hectare thermal park whose spa is fed by a strongly mineralised spring flowing at 36 °C, combining baths, saunas, fitness pavilion and a 4-star superior hotel.
quote: Nestled in a 45-hectare park, the thermal resort combines spa, wellness, fitness, hotels, restaurants, and event venues ... spa installations fed by a strongly mineralised water source flowing at 36°C

claim: Within Schloss Berg itself, Victor's Residenz-Hotel runs two casual sister restaurants — Bacchus (upscale Italian/Mediterranean) and Victor's Landgasthaus Die Scheune — alongside Christian Bau's three-star Fine Dining room.
quote: In the Bacchus restaurant, named after the Roman god of wine, you will experience a culinary journey of pleasure right through upscale Italian cuisine with fine fish and meat variations, light pasta dishes and fantastically sweet desserts.

claim: Hotel-Restaurant Hammes in the village of Perl is a 3-star family-run hotel restaurant in a quiet side street, serving German and international dishes with a strong local wine list, and convenient for cyclists and Moselle visitors.
quote: The hotel is surrounded by romantic cycling and hiking paths, picturesquely situated vineyards, and boundless garden pleasures ... The restaurant focuses on fresh, diverse and natural ingredients to turn eating into an exceptional experience.

claim: Restaurant Niedmühle in Rehlingen-Siersburg sits in the official Michelin Guide for Saarland; it is roughly 30 km from Perl, set directly on the Nied river with a winter garden and terrace.
quote: Niedmühle - Rehlingen-Siersburg Restaurants

claim: The European Museum Schengen reopened in June 2025 with a free, multilingual permanent exhibition on the 1985 Schengen Agreement; the original signing ship MS Princesse Marie-Astrid is moored a short walk away and is open to visitors.
quote: The Schengen Museum reopened in June 2025 ... The modern permanent exhibition offers an engaging and multilingual experience, presenting the history and significance of the Schengen Agreement ... The historic ship "Prinzessin Marie-Astrid Europa", where the Schengen Agreement was signed in 1985, is anchored just a short walk from the museum and open to visitors.

claim: The Deutsches Zeitungsmuseum in Wadgassen lies about 47 km / 26 minutes' drive from Perl, putting it just outside the 30 km radius for this trip.
quote: The distance over roads between Wadgassen and Perl (Mosel) is 29 miles, and it takes approximately 26 minutes to drive.
